attribution.note: Marcus explicitly endorses the negative forecast through his own bet. Musk's probabilistic prediction is background, not the claim being graded.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves Marcus's explicit end-2025 deadline and his definition of superiority as performing any intellectual work any human can do. His bet commits him to a definite outcome.

contract.note: The universal capability threshold comes from Marcus himself. Testing whether AI completes human-solvable reasoning tasks fairly operationalizes that threshold. The contract expressly uses near-deadline public measurements.

evidence.note: The December 5 measurement meets the contract's near-deadline criterion. The best verified commercial and refinement systems scored 37.6% and 54%, respectively. These results show substantial progress but not full completion of the human-solvable task set.

The benchmark authors' preprint establishes human solvability of the evaluation tasks: each was solved by at least two people. This supplies the human-capability side of the comparison, not evidence of December AI performance.

output.rationale: Under the contract's near-deadline measurement rule, the evidence supports the forecast. Human testing establishes that the evaluation tasks are solvable by people, while December results show no verified AI system completing the set. The reported AI advances do not meet Marcus's universal capability threshold. This conclusion is based on verified public performance, not an exhaustive assessment of undisclosed systems.
